evidence.source: 裘錫圭, “甲骨文中的見與視,” 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.field: analysis of oracle-bone and bronze forms; dated examples
evidence.text: The author argues that two Shang oracle-bone graphs formerly both read as 見 should be distinguished: the form with a seated human below 目 is 見, while the form with a standing human is 視. The Guodian Chu slips’ distinct forms for 視 and 見 support that reading. He identifies the standing-figure form in Western Zhou bronzes as 視 too. In Western Zhou inscriptions, the pictographic form continued alongside a form written with 見 and 氏 as phonetic; later regional evidence shows the older pictographic spelling persisted in Chu longer than in Jin. The article also reviews an earlier proposal to read one oracle-bone form as 望, and rejects it.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：甲骨文中的見與視

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說明; 說文釋形; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry records the received Shuowen wording “瞻也。从見、示” and Duan Yucai’s reading “从見，示聲.” It glosses 視 first as looking, then gives attested extended senses including examining or observing, treating someone as, eyesight, caring for, administering, comparing, imitating, and a use通「示」. It cites classical examples, including Analects 為政 for examining conduct and Mencius 離婁 for treating a ruler or minister as a body part. These are dictionary-attested senses; the entry does not by itself establish the chronology or derivational path among them.
evidence.title: [A03769] 視 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 正字; 注音; 漢語拼音
evidence.text: The entry identifies 視 as the standard head character, gives Mandarin ㄕˋ / shì, and cites the Shuowen pronunciation 神至切. Its account locates the character under 見 because 見 is the primary semantic element in the received form.
evidence.title: [A03769] 視 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 entry reproduced by shuowen5.com
evidence.field: 說文原文; 字形演變; 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The page gives the received definition “瞻也。从見、示,” labels 𥄙 and 眡 as ancient forms in the Shuowen tradition, and lists images identified as oracle-bone examples, Western Zhou bronzes, Chu manuscripts, Qin clerical writing and Western Han clerical writing. The page’s Duan Yucai commentary explicitly reads 示 as a phonetic element and discusses other historical uses of 視, including usages in which the graph is used for 示. The page’s catalogue labels do not alone establish dates for each manuscript example.

gaps: The earliest securely interpretable examples are reported as Shang oracle-bone forms, but the inspected article excerpt does not provide an absolute inscription date for a specific 視 token; the Guodian manuscript is associated with a tomb dated broadly to the mid-fourth through early-third century BCE.

No dated primary passage was inspected here that establishes a chronology among 視’s later senses such as ‘observe,’ ‘treat as,’ ‘care for,’ or ‘administer.’ The MOE dictionary supplies examples, not a complete semantic history.

The exact local kMandarin rows for both 視 and 视 were supplied, but official Unicode character-specific pages could not be verified in this session; cite the official records only as attempted URLs, not as inspected evidence.

The packet supplies Baxter–Sagart readings for 視 but not 示. A verified same-system reading for 示 is missing, so the phonetic role is supported here by Duan Yucai’s explicit historical dictionary interpretation, not an independently checked reconstruction comparison.

The proposal that 視’s original pictograph meant seeing because the lower human figure is standing while 見 has a kneeling figure is a scholarly paleographic interpretation grounded in distribution and manuscript contrast; it remains an interpretation, and an older 望 analysis is recorded as disputed.

No exact authoritative standard page for the simplified counterpart relationship 視→视 was inspected. The dossier’s imported statement calls 视 simplified from 視, but this research pass does not independently substantiate that classification.
